$exampleSchema._comment: Example only — documents the shape. The renderer reads `entries`, not this key. Drop entries with newest first. `kind` is one of "feat" | "fix". Date format YYYY-MM-DD.
$exampleSchema.headline: Short tagline shown as the section title

items.text: Description of a new feature.
Description of a bug fix.
A class card's rating now shows "≈" when it comes from the professor's other classes or from other professors, so you can tell it apart from a rating for that exact class.
Schedule combinations now keep a class's lecture and discussion together instead of treating them as either-or.
When no schedule fits your credit range, Combinations says so instead of showing a bare "0 of 0".
The CTEC panel now opens on the same rating the class card shows, instead of a broader view you picked earlier.
On smaller laptop screens, Paper.nu class cards no longer hide the rating behind their buttons, CAESAR's header and Shopping Cart columns fit better, and Course History's Download CSV stays in view.
After Pencil updates, pages you left open ask you to refresh instead of saying CTECs are unavailable.
CTEC analytics now open inside Paper.nu's Section Info panel, on a CTECs tab, with one-click terms, comment search and the phrases students mention most.
When a professor has no CTECs for a class, Pencil lists who else has taught it and what else they teach, one click away.
Pencil has a cleaner look everywhere. Prefer the old colours? Switch back under Theme in this popup.
CTECs no longer say a professor has never taught anything after Pencil loads data in the background.
The sign-in, About and calendar export dialogs are simpler and easier to read.
The Class Search, Cart, Enrollment Dates and Course History shortcuts now open inside CAESAR's own pages, so the top bar and the left-hand tabs stay with you.
Your browser's Back and Forward buttons now move between CAESAR pages, like search results and class details, instead of leaving CAESAR.
Loading seats or searching with Pencil no longer makes CAESAR say "This page is no longer available" on your next click.
CTECs now include a course's evaluations from before it was renumbered or its department was renamed, like COMP_SCI 208 (formerly 214), instead of saying the professor hasn't taught it.
See registration dates and your assigned appointments from the Paper.nu and CAESAR headers, and add appointment start times to Google Calendar.
Prereq trees on Paper.nu now show current course numbers instead of retired ones, and courses you took under an old number still count.
Prereqs written as lists, like "A or B, C or D, and E", are now grouped the way the registrar means them.
Sequence courses such as MATH 220-1 now expand to show their own prereqs.
Prereq trees have a new sideways layout that fits on screen: the course is on the left, and brackets show whether you need all of a group or just one.
Prereq trees no longer show stray sentence fragments as requirements, and grade minimums like "C- or better" now show on every course they apply to.
When CTECs signs you out, Pencil asks you to sign in again instead of showing no ratings or "CTEC unavailable".
After you sign in to CTECs, Pencil picks up where it left off instead of searching for your class again.
Course History now groups your finished classes by term, filters by subject like DSGN or COMP_SCI, and downloads what you see as a CSV.
My courses in the popup shows your grades and lists terms in the right order.
Copy your Paper.nu schedule as Markdown without adding a clipboard permission when Pencil updates.
Pencil shortcuts stay on the right across CAESAR pages, with a CAESAR home logo on the left when the native branding is missing.
Find special-topics sections like Health Tech by name in Sharper Search, with topic names shown in the results.
Click the Pencil icon in CAESAR to learn about Pencil or leave feedback.
If Pencil can’t reach CAESAR, it points you to Northwestern’s VPN setup and lets you retry loading CTECs.
Keep Home and Class Search within reach after choosing a term in the Shopping Cart.
Preview registration dates from the header, then open CAESAR for your assigned time.
The Shopping Cart and Enrollment Dates pages are easier to scan, and a small Pencil mark identifies the added shortcuts.
Jump to Class Search, your cart, enrollment dates, or course history from CAESAR’s header.
Sharper Search remembers your filters, results, and scroll position when you return in the same tab.
Copy your Paper.nu schedule as Markdown, including meeting times and any CTEC ratings you’ve loaded.
Sharper Search opens from the Shopping Cart’s Search button.
Adding a class from Paper.nu uses the right CAESAR quarter, even while you’re searching.
CTECs you've already loaded stay loaded after a refresh, including in the hover preview and Analytics.
Co-taught classes and professors who share a last name now find the right CTECs.
Cross-listed and 400-level courses (like COMP_SCI 497) find their professor's CTECs instead of saying they've never taught it.
Special-topics courses only show CTECs for that exact topic, not the professor's other topics under the same number.
Rating distribution charts show up again.
CTECs load again — Northwestern moved them to a new site and pencil.nu couldn't follow. It can now.

entries.headline: Get your schedule into your calendar

items.text: Export your Paper.nu schedule straight to Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook — a step-by-step walkthrough opens after you hit Download, with one-click jumps to each calendar's import page.
Paper.nu's EXPORT button now glows so you can find it at a glance.
Paper.nu's logo now wears a small "with pencil" tag and a tiny pencil icon — an at-a-glance reminder that the extension is on the page.

entries.headline: See your weekly study load at a glance

items.text: See your estimated weekly out-of-class study hours at the top of Paper.nu — hover for the per-class breakdown.
New "Lazy mode" sort for schedule combinations — lightest workload first.
Paper.nu cart chips now show what you're enrolled in vs. still in your cart.
Changing the schedule-combinations sort jumps back to combo #1.

entries.headline: See CTECs by course or by prof

items.text: See CTECs from a broader angle: every prof who's taught the course, or every course your prof has taught. Pick one and we remember it for that section.
Cross-listed sections (like COMP_SCI 346 / COMP_ENG 346) now show real per-section seat counts instead of the pooled total.
Hide already-taken courses from Paper.nu search with a new switch above the results.
Eligibility checks on Paper.nu catch more prereqs now — they read CAESAR's official requirement text on top of the structured list.

entries.headline: Filter Sharper Search by Foundational Discipline

items.text: Filter Sharper Search by Weinberg's Foundational Disciplines — toggle Nat Sci, Emp Ded, Soc Beh, History, Ethics, or Lit Arts to narrow results, and see at a glance which a course fulfills from the icons on every card.
Searching something like "comp_sci 3" in Sharper Search now lists courses in catalog-number order (300, 305, … 349, …) instead of by title length.

entries.headline: See what you're eligible to take, on Paper.nu

items.text: Paper.nu search now shows little eligibility badges on every course based on what you've already taken in CAESAR — click the chip above the results to hide the ones you can't take yet.
Schedule cards on Paper.nu pick up a small ✓ or ? marker — hover to see what the course is asking for.
Your CAESAR course history is now cached and viewable in the popup under "My courses".

entries.headline: Missing grad year? You're in; schedule combinations

items.text: Cycle every non-overlapping schedule of your Paper.nu classes — pin sections, set a credit range, sort by CTEC rating.
If we couldn't read your expected graduation year from CAESAR, the extension now unlocks anyway instead of holding you back.
Loading CTECs on Sharper Search now signs you in properly instead of getting stuck.
Accessing CTECs on CAESAR normally works now.
Smoother, more consistent CTEC analytics colors.
